verses.text: The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
Yahweh’s word  came to him in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.

It came also in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, to the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah, the son of Josiah, king of Judah, to the carrying away of Jerusalem captive in the fifth month.
Now Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,
“Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you. Before you were born, I sanctified you. I have appointed you a prophet to the nations.”
Then I said, “Ah, Lord  Yahweh! Behold,  I don’t know how to speak; for I am a child.”
But Yahweh said to me, “Don’t say, ‘I am a child;’ for you must go to whomever I send you, and you must say whatever I command you.
Don’t be afraid because of them, for I am with you to rescue you,” says Yahweh.
Then Yahweh stretched out his hand, and touched my mouth. Then Yahweh said to me, “Behold, I have put my words in your mouth.
Behold, I have today set you over the nations and over the kingdoms, to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant.”
Moreover Yahweh’s word came to me, saying, “Jeremiah, what do you see?” I said, “I see a branch of an almond tree.”
Then Yahweh said to me, “You have seen well; for I watch over my word to perform it.”
Yahweh’s word came to me the second time, saying, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a boiling cauldron; and it is tipping away from the north.”
Then Yahweh said to me, “Out of the north, evil will break out on all the inhabitants of the land.

For, behold, I will call all the families of the kingdoms of the north,” says Yahweh. “They will come, and they will each set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, and against all its walls all around, and against all the cities of Judah.
I will utter my judgments against them concerning all their wickedness, in that they have forsaken me, and have burned incense to other gods, and worshiped the works of their own hands.
“You therefore put your belt on your waist, arise, and say to them all that I command you. Don’t be dismayed at them, lest I dismay you before them.

For, behold, I have made you today a fortified city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls, against the whole land, against the kings of Judah, against its princes, against its priests, and against the people of the land.
They will fight against you, but they will not prevail against you; for I am with you”, says Yahweh, “to rescue you.”

footnotes.content: Here is a man marked from the priestly line, from a small town called Anathoth. But the Lord is choosing him for something far stranger than temple service—He's calling a prophet into the heart of a kingdom that will not want to hear him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Josiah was the king who sought the Lord, who tore down idols and called the nation back to God's book. Into that season of reform, Yahweh's word came to young Jeremiah. Sometimes the faithful are called precisely in the twilight, before the darkness deepens.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The list of kings here—Josiah, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah—spans the arc from hope to catastrophe, ending at the fifth month when Jerusalem itself is carried away captive. This is the long, bitter span Jeremiah would witness and proclaim. His word would outlast all their thrones.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now the Lord speaks directly to the young man himself—personal, immediate, not through priests or rituals, but in the deepest privacy of his own heart. 'Now Yahweh's word came to me, saying'—this is the invitation into intimacy with the very God of Israel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before the womb. Before birth. Before memory or choice. The Lord knew Jeremiah and set him apart for this bitter work before time even held him. When we feel small or unsure, this word whispers: you were never a mistake, never an accident. You were known and loved first.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Listen to his honesty—'I don't know how to speak; for I am a child.' No pretense, no false courage. The young man stands before the Almighty and simply tells the truth about his terror and inadequacy. The Lord doesn't shame him for it; He's been waiting for this confession.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord doesn't remove the youth; He redefines the objection. 'Don't say you are a child'—not because it isn't true, but because weakness is no barrier to His calling. The words you'll speak are His words, placed in your mouth. Your youth is no excuse; your fear is no veto.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before Jeremiah speaks a single warning or weeps his first tears, the Lord gives him this anchor: 'Don't be afraid because of them, for I am with you to rescue you.' Not that the path will be easy—it will break his heart—but that he will not be abandoned in it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh stretches out His hand and touches the prophet's mouth—a ritual gesture of commissioning, like the altar coal touching Isaiah's lips. 'I have put my words in your mouth.' The Lord doesn't ask Jeremiah to find eloquence; He supplies it Himself, mouth to mouth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A prophet carries authority over kingdoms—not to conquer with swords, but with words. To uproot, tear down, destroy, overthrow—and also to build and plant. Jeremiah will speak both judgment and hope, and both will prove true. One voice, two ministries, one Lord behind them both.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An almond tree—'shaqed' in Hebrew, which sounds like 'shoqed,' meaning 'watching' or 'waking.' The Lord is showing Jeremiah a living symbol: just as the almond is the first to wake and blossom in spring, so the Lord 'watches over' His word to bring it to pass. A visual sermon, wordless.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord confirms the young prophet's sight: 'You have seen well.' God is not far from His word, careless or distant. He bends close over it, watching to perform it. Every threat and every promise from His lips will come to pass, as surely as the almond wakes each spring.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A second vision—now a cauldron, boiling, tipping from the north. The image is visceral, unsettling. Jeremiah is shown not abstract theology but the raw reality: danger is coming, judgment is heating, and it will pour out of the north toward Judah. Not to terrify him, but to make him see clearly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord interprets the vision plainly: 'Out of the north, evil will break out.' No riddles now, no symbols to puzzle over. Jeremiah must understand what he's been sent to announce. The Babylonians will come, and it will be the judgment of the Lord Himself against a people who have turned from Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord will summon the northern kingdoms like an army of servants, and they will lay siege to Jerusalem itself. Thrones will be set at the gates, walls surrounded. Jeremiah will live to see this very thing come to pass—not as a prophet's flight of fancy, but as bitter historical reality.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The reason for judgment is clear: the people have forsaken the Lord, burned incense to other gods, worshiped the work of their own hands. Not arbitrary cruelty, but the harvest of apostasy. The Lord speaks His judgments because He is faithful to His covenant—unfaithfulness has consequence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now comes the charge: 'Put your belt on your waist'—prepare yourself, take your stand. Say all that the Lord commands, hold nothing back. And again, the shield: 'Don't be dismayed at them, lest I dismay you.' His fear is worse than theirs; His presence stronger than their opposition.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A fortified city, an iron pillar, bronze walls—the Lord is saying, I will make you immovable, unbreakable in spirit. Not that your enemies won't come; they will. But you will not fall. Against kings and priests and people, you will stand because I am your foundation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo of something deeper: 'They will fight against you, but they will not prevail.' The world will always press hard against those who speak the Lord's truth. But the assurance stands—His presence, His rescue, His faithfulness. In every age, the faithful prophet is not left orphaned.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
